observed_control_flow: The Vulkan runtime allocates b_exec148 with kExecFamilyBytes before execution-arm routing.
It materializes all 14 Q4-down target tensors into b_exec148 before any A/B/AB arm is executed.
The same process subsequently executes arm A and arm B.
The fresh W-S result records exec148_incremental_bytes=549527552 while arm A also executes successfully.
binding_drift_evidence.violated_frozen_invariant: A route / lifecycle NONE must not cause B representation acquisition.

stop_rule.reason: A preregistered fail condition is structural and workload-independent: backend representation acquisition occurs even when policy would route A with lifecycle NONE.

scientific_interpretation.meaning: Frozen v4 correctly distinguishes routing from acquisition; the current Q4-down Vulkan harness violates that distinction by pre-materializing B. This is backend implementation drift, not evidence that the six-part generic abstraction is incomplete.

requirements: Do not allocate/materialize EXEC148 when policy lifecycle is NONE and route is A.
Allocate/materialize exactly once on ACQUIRE_B selected by v4.
Expose B as execution_ready only after identity validation succeeds.
Release B only on EVICT_B or explicit teardown consistent with frozen lifecycle.
Do not add hidden retry/fallback inside the backend adapter.
Keep generic policy and binding core family-agnostic.
